source_snapshot.items: Configuring BMC Network through IPMI for static(IB)
source_snapshot.procedure: Through in-band IPMI set verified channel source to static, then IP address, netmask and default gateway; eth0/eth1 are described as channels 1/2.
source_snapshot.criteria: Commands return no error and complete `lan print` values are correct.
source_snapshot.script: No script; 10 attended and 10 machine minutes; setup requests clearing logs.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL but assumes channel 1 and invents 192.168.0.50/24, omits gateway validation and uses command-line BMC credentials over the changing path.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at HIGH risk; resolve IB/channel mapping, IPAM tuple, complete baseline, alternate recovery, one-channel mutation, full-state reconnect and rollback.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes disconnect risk but turns source placeholders into executable network values and validates only a filtered subset of the resulting LAN state.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly makes IPAM, exact channel identity, alternate access and full reversible configuration mandatory before mutation.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The in-band path is important because it can remain usable while the BMC address changes, but it does not remove the risk of configuring the wrong physical interface. Channel number, BMC MAC and port/VLAN identity must be correlated before any write, and the old tuple must be restorable without relying on the new address.

original_test_intent: Configure one verified BMC interface with an approved static IP, netmask and gateway through in-band IPMI, then prove the complete persistent LAN state and reachability.
original_method: Capture and hash the full current LAN configuration, bind IPMI channel to physical BMC port/MAC/VLAN, validate an IPAM-approved nonconflicting tuple and alternate recovery, apply each field on the one approved channel, reconnect via the new address, compare complete `lan print` and restore the baseline if retention is not approved.
manual_activity: The network/BMC owner supplies the exact channel and IPAM tuple, approves the disconnect and retention/rollback policy; an operator maintains console or alternate OOB recovery throughout the change.
required_inputs: Meaning of IB and supported in-band transport
Conflict, ARP, VLAN and route validation
safety_requirements: Never use source placeholders or DeepSeek's sample address
Stop on conflict, wrong port, ambiguous completion or failed reconnect
Rollback under owner direction without automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Apply source/address/netmask/gateway one field at a time
Verify new-path reachability and target identity
Restore if required and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Decide whether the static state persists

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The `lan set` family matches the test, but channel 1 and 192.168.0.50 are invented, the default gateway is omitted and filtered output cannot establish VLAN, MAC, auth/cipher or complete post-state.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through the verified in-band transport, apply `ipsrc static`, owner-approved IP, netmask and default gateway to the mapped channel only, retaining complete unfiltered pre/post `lan print` and validated reconnect/rollback evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 10/10-minute scope and four static-setting operations remain; all placeholders stay unresolved until owner/IPAM input and no diagnostic logs are cleared.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a configuration transaction record containing channel/port/MAC identity, full before state, approved tuple, each write result, address-change timeline, full after state, reachability identity proof and rollback result.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Eliminates guessed values and partial verification while adding alternate recovery and exact physical-channel provenance.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Command success and three grepped fields do not prove gateway, VLAN, MAC, auth/cipher or that the intended interface was changed.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some BMCs apply fields asynchronously or reset sessions; post-state polling must be bounded and must not treat temporary old-address reachability as persistence.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define whether the new static tuple remains after the testcase. Any multi-channel migration, VLAN change, credential/auth change or network-service restart is outside this row and needs separate approval.
expected_evidence: Approval, exact channel/port/MAC/VLAN and IPAM tuple
Conflict/route checks and complete baseline hash
Redacted per-field results and application timing
New-path reachability with target identity and alternate-path evidence
Rollback or retained-state proof, BMC health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target static BMC LAN configuration. Blank channel and tuple placeholders are mandatory owner inputs, not competing source scopes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Mapping, IPAM tuple and recovery are normal project inputs. Execution blocks if the only management path would be changed or exact channel/rollback cannot be proven.

review_improvement: Prevents a guessed channel/address from stranding the BMC and upgrades filtered command success into a complete identity-bound configuration transaction with recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: IPMI channel numbering is firmware-specific and not reliably inferred from Linux eth names. Static IP fields can apply at different times, so the session may drop between writes. Binding the channel to MAC/port first and using an in-band control path plus independent recovery keeps partial application observable and reversible.
